actions.justification: Mandatory first step — assess current hemodynamic stability in a patient with palpitations and dizziness. Mechanical heart valve increases risk of serious complications.
Mandatory — identify rhythm disturbance (e.g., atrial fibrillation, flutter, SVT) as the cause of palpitations and dizziness. Critical for diagnosis and treatment planning.
Mandatory — patient has mechanical heart valve and hypertension, both of which confer high thromboembolic risk. CHA2DS2-VASc score required to guide anticoagulation decisions.

MANDATORY: BMP is required to assess electrolytes (hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia can cause arrhythmias), renal function (important for medication dosing and anticoagulation management), and glucose. Critical in a patient with palpitations and hypertension.
MANDATORY: TSH is required to evaluate for thyroid dysfunction, which is a common reversible cause of atrial arrhythmias presenting with palpitations and dizziness.
Patient with palpitations and a mechanical heart valve requires continuous cardiac monitoring to detect arrhythmias, rate changes, or hemodynamic deterioration while awaiting lab results.

Patient has a mechanical heart valve, which is a high-risk condition requiring careful anticoagulation management. With palpitations and dizziness, possible atrial fibrillation or arrhythmia must be evaluated in context of anticoagulation status to prevent thromboembolic complications.

Patient with mechanical heart valve presenting with palpitations and dizziness requires urgent cardiology input to guide management of potential arrhythmia and ensure appropriate anticoagulation therapy for their high-risk valvular condition.

Patient has a mechanical heart valve, which is a strong indication for anticoagulation. In the setting of new palpitations/possible atrial fibrillation with a mechanical valve, heparin bridging is indicated to prevent thromboembolic complications while further workup is completed.

Patient presents with palpitations and dizziness with underlying mechanical heart valve and hypertension. Electrophysiology consultation is warranted to guide arrhythmia management and rhythm control strategy given the complexity of anticoagulation needs with a mechanical valve.

If the ECG reveals atrial fibrillation or another tachyarrhythmia requiring rate control, rate control medication is indicated to manage symptoms of palpitations and dizziness while maintaining hemodynamic stability.

Order a follow-up ECG to assess current rhythm status and response to rate control, given the patient has palpitations with a mechanical heart valve and hypertension. This is distinct from the initial 12-lead ECG already obtained.

Echocardiogram is indicated to assess mechanical valve function, rule out structural abnormalities, and evaluate for thrombus or valve dysfunction contributing to palpitations and dizziness in this high-risk patient.
Chest X-ray is part of the standard workup for palpitations and dizziness to assess cardiac silhouette, pulmonary vasculature, and rule out pulmonary congestion or other contributing pathology.
CBC is indicated to evaluate for anemia (which can cause palpitations and dizziness) and to assess baseline hematologic status in a patient with mechanical heart valve on anticoagulation.
Patient has a mechanical heart valve requiring anticoagulation therapy. Coagulation studies (INR/PT) are critical to assess therapeutic anticoagulation levels and guide management.

Echocardiogram is indicated to evaluate mechanical valve function, assess for structural abnormalities, and evaluate for underlying causes of palpitations in this high-risk patient with a mechanical heart valve.
Patient has a mechanical heart valve requiring anticoagulation monitoring. INR is critical to assess therapeutic anticoagulation status and guide management of this high-risk patient.
Renal function assessment is important to guide medication dosing (e.g., anticoagulants, rate control agents) and evaluate any metabolic contributors to the presentation.
Assess for tissue hypoperfusion given the patient's palpitations and dizziness, to exclude hemodynamic compromise despite currently stable vitals.
Patient with palpitations, dizziness, hypertension, and mechanical heart valve requires troponin to rule out acute myocardial injury as a contributing cause of arrhythmia.
NT-proBNP will help assess for heart failure or elevated filling pressures, which can precipitate or exacerbate arrhythmia in this patient with hypertension and mechanical valve.

Patient has a mechanical heart valve, which is a mandatory indication for anticoagulation. Ensuring therapeutic anticoagulation is critical given the ongoing arrhythmia and thromboembolic risk associated with mechanical valves.

Patient has palpitations and dizziness with a mechanical heart valve and hypertension. Rate control is a priority in arrhythmia management. Beta-blocker can help control heart rate and manage palpitations while awaiting pending lab results (INR, CBC, troponin). HR is currently 80 which is acceptable, but beta-blocker supports ongoing rate control strategy already initiated.
